schema:alternativeHeadline:
An Indian Pueblos population and feast-date card is mounted beside a photograph of people outside a hotel and restaurant and a Mrs. Wilson’s Tea Shop card for Zuni, New Mexico.

Written text (transcribed as written):
Left card: “INDIAN PUEBLOS—Population and Date of Their Feasts in New Mexico Census of 1920 Acoma—841—Sept. 1st Cochiti—244—July 14th Isleta—749—Aug. 28th Jemes—508—Nov. 12th Laguna—1719—Sept. 1st Nambey—87—Oct 4th Picuris—93—Aug. 10th Pojoaque—9—Dec. 12th San Felipe—532—May 1st San Ildefonso—81—Jan. 23rd San Juan—293—June 24th Sandia—92—June 13th Santa Ana—200—Aug. Santa Clara—246—Aug. 12 Santo Domingo—780—Aug. 4th Taos—571—Sept. 29th Tesuque—109—Nov. 12th Zia—110—Aug. 15th Zuni—1842—Nov. Moon Genuine Navajo, Balleta and Chimayo Blankets, Pottery and Bead Work.”
Upper right sign cut off by photograph edge: “HOTEL & RESTAU[cut off]”
Lower right business card: “Mrs. Wilson's Tea Shop At Vanderwagons' Store ZUNI, N. M. Lunch Boxes Packed Meals and Short Orders Comfortable Rooms Artists Studio in Connection”
